## 1. Who must make estimated payments

Estimated payments are required when the expected tax, after withholding and credits, exceeds $500. This applies to residents and nonresidents alike.

- MCL 206.301(1), source 5: "if the person's annual tax can reasonably be expected to exceed the amount withheld under section 351 and the credits allowed under this part by more than $500.00".
- MI-1040ES, TY2026, source 1: "You must make estimated income tax payments if you expect to owe more than $500 when you file your 2026 MI-1040 return."

Filing status: the threshold is the same for all statuses. Married couples who will file separately must make separate payments.

- MI-1040ES, TY2026, source 1: "separate vouchers and payments must be submitted for each filer."

## 2. Required annual payment

Michigan follows IRC § 6654. The required annual payment is the lesser of:

- 90% of the current year's tax (66 2/3% for farmers, fishermen and seafarers), or
- 100% of the prior year's tax, or 110% if prior-year AGI was more than $150,000 ($75,000 married filing separately).

- MI-1040ES, TY2026, source 1: "110 percent of your total 2025 tax if your 2025 adjusted gross income is more than $150,000 ($75,000 for married filing separately)."
- MI-2210, TY2025, source 2: "110 percent of the tax shown on your 2024 return if 2024 Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) was more than $150,000 if filing joint or single ($75,000 if your 2024 filing status is married filing separately)."

Filed return and 12-month year: the prior-year option requires both.

- RAB 2021-17, source 3: "100% of the tax shown on the preceding-year return, if the taxpayer filed a return and the return was for a 12-month tax year."

The 110% rule does not apply to farmers, fishermen or seafarers.

- RAB 2021-17, source 3: "The 110% rule does not apply to farmers and fishermen or to seafarers for Michigan purposes".

High-income taxpayers do not lose the prior-year option; they use 110%.

MCL 206.301(11) adopts the federal computation.

- MCL 206.301(11), source 5: "computed, payment of estimated tax shall be credited, and a period of underpayment shall be determined in the same manner as provided in the internal revenue code."

## 3. Due dates and shares

There are four equal installments of 25%, due April 15, June 15 and September 15 of the tax year and January 15 of the next year.

- MCL 206.301(1), source 5: "each installment shall be equal to 1/4 the taxpayer's estimated tax".
- MI-1040ES, TY2026, source 1: "in equal installments due on or before April 15, 2026, June 15, 2026, September 15, 2026, and January 15, 2027."

Weekend and holiday shift (corrected in verification): a due date on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday moves to the next day that is none of these. The rule is MCL 8.6, which applies to all Michigan statutes. The 2025 MI-2210 applies it: June 15, 2025 was a Sunday, so the second due date is "June 16, 2025". None of the 2026 due dates falls on a weekend (April 15 is a Wednesday, June 15 a Monday, September 15 a Tuesday, January 15, 2027 a Friday).

- MCL 8.6, source 10: "a fixed or final day is a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, the period or day is extended".

January waiver: if the return is filed and paid by January 31, no penalty is charged on the fourth installment. Interest is still charged (see answer 10).

- RAB 2021-17, source 3: "no penalty is imposed for any underpayment of a Q4 estimated payment if the taxpayer files a return for the taxable year on or before January 31".
- MI-1040ES, TY2026, source 1: "you may file your 2026 income tax return before February 1, 2027, instead."

## 4. Withholding

By default, one-fourth of the year's withholding is treated as paid on each due date. The taxpayer may document the actual dates instead.

- MI-2210, TY2025, source 2: "One-fourth of your total withholding is considered paid on each due date unless you can document the dates the tax was withheld."

## 5. Exceptions with no penalty

- Tax below an amount: no penalty or interest if the tax after withholding and credits is $500 or less. MI-2210, TY2025, source 2: "The total tax on your 2025 return minus the amount you paid in withholding and all your credits is $500 or less."
- No liability in the prior year: no penalty. MI-2210, TY2025, source 2: "You had no tax liability for 2024 (if you had to file), or you were not required to file a 2024 return". If a 12-month prior-year return was filed showing $0 tax, there is no interest either (corrected in verification): the required annual payment is the lesser of 90% of current tax and 100% of $0, so MI-2210 line 7 is $0 and no installment is underpaid.
- Not required to pay estimates in the prior year: no penalty, but interest still applies. MI-2210, TY2025, source 2: "No penalty is charged if estimates were not required in the immediately preceding year; however, interest may still be due." Statute: MCL 205.24(6), source 7.
- First-year residents and part-year residents (corrected in verification): there is no residency-specific rule. A new resident is usually covered by two general exceptions. First, no penalty if the person was not required to file a prior-year Michigan return and the prior-year federal return covered 12 months (MI-2210, source 2). Second, no penalty if estimates were not required in the prior year (MCL 205.24(6), source 7). Interest may still apply under the second. Estimate requirements apply "whether or not you are a Michigan resident" (MI-1040ES, source 1).
- Farmers, fishermen and seafarers (at least two-thirds of gross income from these activities): pay one installment by January 15, or file and pay the return by March 1 with no estimate. The rate is 66 2/3%. MI-1040ES, TY2026, source 1: "File your 2026 MI-1040 return on or before March 1, 2027, and pay the entire tax with the return."
- Retired or disabled: NOT FOUND (confirmed in verification). There is no Michigan counterpart to the federal waiver for retirement after 62 or disability. Searched the sources listed in the verification section.
- Casualty or disaster (corrected in verification): there is no standing rule. Treasury grants relief per event, by notice, after a governor's emergency declaration. Relief is not automatic; the taxpayer must ask. It extends deadlines and waives penalty and interest. Notice of March 19, 2026, source 14: "Any relief provided under this Notice will be effectuated by waiving penalties and interest."
- Reasonable cause (added in verification): a written request can waive the penalty, but not the interest. RAB 2025-15 lists death or serious illness, and records destroyed "by fire or other casualty" (source 12). Statute: MCL 205.23(3), source 6.

## 6. Annualised income method

Allowed, using the Annualized Income Worksheet on Form MI-2210. The periods match federal (3, 5, 8 and 12 months) and so do the percentages (22.5%, 45%, 67.5%, 90%). Recapture applies.

- MI-2210, TY2025, source 2: "If you receive income unevenly during the year ... you may annualize your income."
- MI-2210, TY2025, source 2: "You must annualize for the entire year by completing all four columns."

## 7. How the penalty is computed

There are two separate charges.

**Interest.** Interest is daily, on each installment's shortfall, from the due date to the payment date or April 15, whichever is earlier. Payments are applied to the oldest underpayment first. The rate is the adjusted prime rate plus 1 point, reset January 1 and July 1.

- MCL 205.23(2), source 6: "the same current monthly interest rate of 1 percentage point above the adjusted prime rate per annum from the time the payment was due, until paid."

Rates, from RAB 2026-5 (source 4):

- January 1 to June 30, 2025: 9.47%
- July 1 to December 31, 2025: 8.66%
- January 1 to June 30, 2026: 8.48% (daily 0.0002324)
- July 1 to December 31, 2026: 7.85% (daily 0.0002150)
- January 1 to June 30, 2027: 7.77% (daily 0.0002129), from RAB 2026-10, source 11 (corrected in verification: this period covers the 2026 fourth installment and interest to April 15, 2027).

- RAB 2026-5, source 4: "A daily rate of interest of 0.0002150 based on an adjusted annual rate of 7.85% will be added".
- RAB 2026-10, source 11: "A daily rate of interest of 0.0002129 based on an adjusted annual rate of 7.77% will be added".

Use the published daily rate, not the annual rate divided by 365 (added in verification). For two periods they differ in the seventh decimal place: 8.48% / 365 = 0.0002323 (published 0.0002324), and 7.85% / 365 = 0.0002151 (published 0.0002150). The published daily rates match unrounded annual rates of about 8.483% and 7.848%. Days are counted excluding the due date and including the payment date (RAB 2026-5 example; MCL 8.6).

**Flat penalty.** In addition to interest, there is a flat penalty for each quarter:

- 25% of the quarter's underpayment (minimum $25) if no estimate was paid for that period.
- 10% (minimum $10) if the estimate was too small or late.

For the penalty, payments apply in the quarter received and are never carried back.

- MI-2210, TY2025, source 2: "Penalty is 25 percent of the tax due (minimum $25 per quarter) for failing to file estimated payments or 10 percent (minimum $10 per quarter) for failing to pay enough".
- MI-2210, TY2025, source 2: "Payments are not carried back to offset underpayments in previous quarters."

Statutory basis: MCL 205.23(3) (10%) and 205.23(4) (25%), sources 3 and 6.

Form: MI-2210 (Part 2 for interest, Part 3 for penalty).

## 8. Differences from federal that would surprise

- On top of interest, Michigan charges a flat penalty of 10% or 25% per quarter, with $10 and $25 minimums.
- A late payment cures the interest on earlier quarters, but not the penalty.
- Filing by January 31 removes only the Q4 penalty, not the Q4 interest.
- There is no penalty, though there is interest, if estimates were not required the previous year.
- The interest rate is prime plus 1, reset every six months.
- The threshold is $500.
- Seafarers are treated like farmers.

## 9. Local income taxes

Some Michigan cities levy their own income tax with separate estimated payments.

- Detroit's is administered by the state Treasury. Treasury requires estimates from Detroit filers who expect to owe more than $100 (Form 5123). The Detroit page's withholding note refers to 2023 and 2022 (source 9).
- Detroit rules for 2026 (corrected in verification; the web page is stale, the 2026 Form 5123 governs). Safe harbor: withholding of at least 70% of the lesser of the 2026 tax or the 2025 tax. Due dates: April 15, June 15 and September 15, 2026, and January 15, 2027. Penalty: 1% per month on the unpaid balance, up to 25% of the total tax due. Interest: the state rate. Treasury computes both and sends a bill. Rates: 2.4% residents, 1.2% nonresidents. Form 5123, source 15: "at least 70 percent of the lesser of your total 2026 tax or your total 2025 tax."
- Flint moves to Treasury administration starting with tax year 2026 (effective January 1, 2027).
- Other cities administer their own taxes under the uniform city income tax ordinance (added in verification). Individuals must declare estimated tax when it exceeds $100 (MCL 141.662). Self-administered cities use the last day of the 4th, 6th, 9th and 13th months (April 30, June 30, September 30, January 31). Cities with a Treasury agreement use the 15th of those months (MCL 141.663, source 16). Penalty rules for each city were not researched.

- City Tax page, source 8: "the Michigan Department of Treasury is currently processing City of Detroit Business, Fiduciary, and Individual Income tax returns."
- Detroit estimated payments page, source 9: "Detroit city residents and nonresidents with a city tax liability who expect to owe more than $100".

## 10. Ambiguities and conflicts

- January relief: RAB 2021-17 says "on or before January 31", while MI-1040ES says "before February 1". These are the same date. RAB Example 6 shows that Q4 interest still runs from January 15 even when the penalty is excused.
- Weekend shifting is shown in the MI-2210 date headings (June 16, 2025) but not stated as a rule in any source found. Resolved in verification: MCL 8.6 is the rule (answer 3).
- MI-2210 line 4 on the form says to subtract certain lines "from line 20" of the 2024 MI-1040, while the instructions say "from line 21". The two disagree on which line is the 2024 tax. Resolved in verification: the form is right. On the 2024 MI-1040, line 20 is "Income Tax" and line 21 is voluntary contributions (source 17). The 2025 MI-1040 added an organ donation credit, which moved income tax to line 21; the instructions use the new number by mistake.
- The penalty exception for the "immediately preceding year" (MCL 205.24(6)) is broader than the federal no-liability exception. The MI-2210 also lists a separate no-liability exception. Neither exception removes interest. Corrected in verification: MCL 205.24(6) removes only the penalty, and the MI-2210 confirms interest may still be due. The no-liability exception removes interest too when a $0 prior-year return was filed, because the required payment is then $0 (answer 5). When no prior-year return was required, the 100% option is unavailable and no source says whether interest applies.
- Whether Michigan adopts the federal § 6654(e)(3) waivers (casualty, disaster, retirement after 62, disability) through MCL 206.301(11) is not stated. NOT FOUND. Treasury's estimated-payment and penalty FAQ pages list a "How do I request a penalty waiver?" question, but its answer did not load when fetched. Partly resolved in verification: the FAQ answer loads now. It describes a written reasonable-cause request under RAB 2025-15, which waives penalty only. Disasters are handled by per-event notices (answer 5). No source says § 6654(e)(3) applies.

### Conflicts resolved

1. MI-2210 line 4, line 20 against line 21. The form governs. On the 2024 MI-1040, line 20 is "Income Tax" and lines 25, 26, 27b, 28 and 29 are the refundable credits the form names. Line 21 is voluntary contributions. The instructions use the 2025 numbering by mistake.
2. Weekend shifting. MCL 8.6 governs. The MI-2210 June 16, 2025 heading applies it.
3. Interest under the prior-year exceptions. MCL 205.24(6) bars only the penalty, and the MI-2210 says interest may still be due. Under the no-liability exception with a filed 12-month return, the 100%-of-prior-year option makes the required payment $0, so no interest arises. Still open: whether interest applies when no prior-year return was required. No public source says.
4. Daily interest factors. For January to June 2026 the form and RAB print 0.0002324, but 8.48% / 365 = 0.0002323. For July to December 2026 the RAB prints 0.0002150, but 7.85% / 365 = 0.0002151. The factors imply unrounded annual rates of about 8.483% and 7.848%. Use the published factor. The error is under $0.01 per $1,000 per 100 days.
5. Detroit web page against the 2026 Form 5123. The form is for 2026; the page is stale.
6. New, unresolved and minor: MI-2210 2025 says column D covers payments "through January 15, 2026", and also that payments "received after January 16, 2026" are not estimates. The status of a payment made on January 16 is unclear.
7. New, minor: MI-1040ES 2026 and MI-2210 2025 point to RAB 2025-13 for rates. That bulletin has since been replaced by RAB 2026-5 and then RAB 2026-10.

No statute was amended in 2024, 2025 or 2026. The latest amendments are MCL 206.301 by 2011 PA 38, MCL 205.23 by 1993 PA 14, and MCL 205.24 by 2003 PA 201. RAB 2021-17 has not been replaced. The 2024, 2025 and 2026 bulletin lists contain no new estimated-payment bulletin for individuals.

### NOT FOUND items

- First-year and part-year residents: filled (answer 5). No residency-specific rule exists.
- Casualty or disaster: filled (answer 5). Relief is per event, by notice and on request.
- Retired or disabled (§ 6654(e)(3)(B)): confirmed NOT FOUND. Searched: MI-1040ES 2026; MI-2210 2025 form and instructions; RAB 2021-17; RAB 2025-15; Treasury FAQ "How do I request a penalty waiver?" and the IIT penalties and interest page; MCL 206.301, 205.23, 205.24; Treasury RAB lists for 2024, 2025 and 2026; web searches of michigan.gov and legislature.mi.gov. Mich Admin Code R 205.1012 and R 205.1013 (reasonable cause) are cited by RAB 2025-15 but were not read from the official code site.

### 2026 changes

- Income tax rate for 2026: 4.25%, unchanged. Treasury notice, source 13: "the rate in effect under Section 51 for the 2026 tax year is 4.25%." The MI-1040ES worksheet also uses 4.25%.
- Interest: 8.48% for January to June 2026, 7.85% for July to December 2026, and 7.77% for January to June 2027 (RAB 2026-10, approved September 30, 2026).
- No statute change to the threshold, percentages, dates or penalty.
- No 2026 due date falls on a weekend or holiday. February 1, 2027 and March 1, 2027 are Mondays.
- 2026 disaster notices: March 2026 winter weather (7 counties, deadlines through April 30, 2026); July 2026 flooding (Antrim, Cheboygan, Emmet, deadlines through August 6, 2026). Both require a request. Neither names the April 15, 2026 individual estimate explicitly.
- Flint moves to Treasury administration for tax year 2026, effective January 1, 2027.
- The 2026 MI-2210 is not yet published. The TY2026 URL returned 404. Answers 4 to 7 rely on the 2025 form.
